_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x21-rb-input.json and judged every hint independently, without opening any other file, searching the repository or using the web.

hints.reason: Clean double meaning: an ambulance's wailing siren, and the mythic Sirens whose song lured sailors, a familiar myth with a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the myth sense is widely known and the text is accurate.

hints.reason: Two famous Buzzes: Apollo 11 astronaut Buzz Aldrin and the Toy Story toy Buzz Lightyear, who is himself a space ranger, so the pair clicks neatly.

pairs.pair_note: Top-tier hint; facts are correct.

hints.reason: The classic 'Banana who? ... Orange you glad I didn't say banana?' knock-knock joke uses both targets, a playful and instantly familiar route that beats the flat FRUIT.

pairs.pair_note: Hyphenated hint is allowed; a fun, broadly known reference.

hints.reason: Clear double meaning: a strike in baseball and striking a match to light it.
hints.fix: You strike a match to light it, and in baseball a strike can be a missed swing, a foul ball or a called pitch in the zone.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; the explanation's 'a strike is a missed swing or a called pitch' leaves out foul balls, so soften it to 'can be'.

hints.reason: Yogi Bear for BEAR, and his home Jellystone Park for JELLY, a well-known cartoon detail that gives a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect route; Jellystone is familiar to most U.S. players (also the campground chain).

hints.reason: Black Friday gives BLACK, and Black Friday is the day after Thanksgiving, an easy but satisfying link.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and clean; text accurate.

hints.reason: Body double and stunt double are both instantly familiar film stand-ins, so the phrase-join has a shared theme rather than being arbitrary.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase-join worth keeping because both phrases are from the same film world.

hints.reason: A curtsy is the bent-knee counterpart of a bow, and it is the traditional greeting for a queen; both sides are direct.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and pleasant; BOW's other senses (ribbon, archery) add a little misdirection.

hints.reason: A scrub brush for BRUSH, and scrub (scrubland) as low bushy growth for BUSH; the vegetation sense is a little less top-of-mind but well known.

pairs.pair_note: Nice bonus: 'brush' itself also means low undergrowth, so the link is tighter than it first looks.

hints.reason: A tall building (with many stories) and a tall story, a.k.a. tall tale; the stories-of-a-building wordplay adds an extra click.

pairs.pair_note: Americans say 'tall tale' more often, but 'tall story' is understood; not a familiarity problem.

hints.reason: LEAP is a synonym of JUMP, and a leap year adds February 29 to the calendar, an honest second connection.

pairs.pair_note: The synonym is fine here; 'roughly every four years' is properly hedged.

hints.reason: Cap'n Crunch is both a cartoon captain and the cereal he fronts; a cereal-mascot link most U.S. players get instantly.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean; text accurate.

hints.reason: Aladdin's magic carpet for CARPET, and flying on it (A Whole New World) for FLY; very familiar Disney imagery.

pairs.pair_note: FLY's other senses (insect, trouser fly) give some misdirection; fine.

hints.reason: Prince Charming gives CHARM, and he is Cinderella's prince in popular retellings; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Explanation correctly hedges 'widely known as'; Disney's 1950 film mostly just calls him the Prince.

hints.reason: Giant pandas are native only to China, and they are famous zoo stars on loan from China; both links are true and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: A place-plus-setting link in the PENGUIN mould; facts accurate.

hints.reason: The Arctic Circle for CIRCLE, and the Arctic as the far north around the North Pole for NORTH; straightforward.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and accurate.

hints.reason: ZIP code for CODE, and ZIP codes are how U.S. mail is sorted for MAIL; a tight, everyday link.

pairs.pair_note: Zone Improvement Plan expansion is correct.

hints.reason: Spurs are iconic cowboy gear and they strap on at the boot heel; both sides are concrete and true.

pairs.pair_note: BOOT would also work (cowboy boot, boot heel), but SPUR is more specific and equally good.

hints.reason: A crown sits on the head (and the crown is the top of the head) for CROWN; HEAVY comes via the popular saying 'heavy is the head that wears the crown,' which is familiar but HEAD alone may not pull HEAVY off a busy board.

pairs.pair_note: Close call between PASS and BORDERLINE: the saying is widespread in U.S. pop culture, but HEAD is a broad word and the HEAVY side relies on that one phrase. Shakespeare attribution in the line is accurate (Henry IV, Part 2).

hints.reason: Clean double meaning: a blind date and window blinds.
hints.fix: Window blinds are shades, often slatted, that cover a window.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the WINDOW line implies all blinds are slatted (roller blinds are not), so soften it.

hints.reason: Flambe literally means 'flamed', giving FLAME, and classic flambe desserts like bananas Foster and cherries jubilee give DESSERT.

pairs.pair_note: FLAMBE is not a substring of FLAME, but it is so close in spelling and meaning that the FLAME side is nearly a giveaway; still a fair, honest link to both. Worth a second opinion on whether the near-identity is acceptable.

hints.reason: Lab as a Labrador retriever and lab as a science laboratory, a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and accurate.

hints.reason: Garden gnomes for GARDEN, and gnomes as dwarf-like little bearded folklore figures for DWARF.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; text accurate.

hints.reason: Both END and WELL come only via the title All's Well That Ends Well; SHAKESPEARE evokes many words (Romeo, Hamlet, rose, stage), so reaching two plain function-like words takes real effort even though it clicks once seen.

pairs.pair_note: True and fair, just a long way from the hint word to the two targets; no clearly better one-word hint comes to mind. If shipped, note it overlaps the Shakespeare theme of the ROSE hint in this batch.

hints.reason: Hermes the Greek messenger god for GOD, and Hermes the French luxury fashion house (Birkin bags, silk scarves) for FASHION; a satisfying name collision.

pairs.pair_note: The brand is well known even to non-shoppers. HERMES is also used for SHOE + WING in this batch; avoid placing both on related boards.

hints.reason: The fly of a pair of pants usually closes with a zipper, so ZIPPER reaches FLY (trouser sense) and PANTS directly.

pairs.pair_note: Fair and easy but flat, because the two targets are already the same object; acceptable as an easy clue.

hints.reason: Dr. Seuss's Fox in Socks is a title made of the two targets themselves, and it is a widely read U.S. children's book.

pairs.pair_note: SEUSS points to many words (cat, hat, egg, ham), but with FOX and SOCK both on the board the title snaps into place.

hints.reason: Olive Garden is the famous Italian-American chain, linking GARDEN through the brand, and olives are a staple of Italian cooking for OLIVE.

pairs.pair_note: GARDEN only connects through the brand name, but the brand is so familiar that the pair clicks.

hints.reason: Santa brings gifts for GIFT, and the Secret Santa gift swap gives SECRET, with gifts tying both sides together.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and well themed.

hints.reason: Rapunzel's famously long hair, let down from the tower and climbed like a rope, delivers both targets in one image.

pairs.pair_note: Lines correctly treat the rope as a use, not literal rope.

hints.reason: A song's hook is its catchy part (and a fishing hook catches), and a catchy song sticks in your head; both sides connect directly.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant; the 'catch' echo with a fishing hook is a nice touch.

hints.reason: Royal jelly for JELLY, and QUEEN both as royalty and as the queen bee raised on royal jelly, so the hint lands twice on QUEEN.

pairs.pair_note: Bee facts are accurate and properly hedged ('in abundance'); a real aha.

hints.reason: The four-leaf clover gives LEAF and is the classic symbol of LUCK.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and accurate.

hints.reason: Litter box and sandbox are both instantly familiar compounds, and both are boxes of loose granules, which makes the phrase-join satisfying rather than arbitrary.

pairs.pair_note: BOX is a broad compound-maker, but the pairing is natural and fair.

hints.reason: CREAM reaches OREO via its creme filling, but reaches MIDDLE only through the Oreo picture; CREAM on its own does not suggest MIDDLE.

pairs.pair_note: FILLING links MIDDLE more directly (a filling is what sits in the middle) while keeping the Oreo route; CREAM is not wrong, just weak on one side.

hints.reason: Cat and mouse for MOUSE, and the proverb 'when the cat's away, the mice will play' for PLAY.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, broadly known proverb; text accurate.

hints.reason: PowerPoint is the Microsoft Office presentation app for OFFICE, and its decks are made of slides for SLIDE.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and accurate.

hints.reason: A pilot is a TV show's first, test episode, and a season is a run of episodes; the TV sense of PILOT gives a small aha.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; the airline sense of PILOT provides mild misdirection.

hints.reason: PADAWAN is the Star Wars word for a Jedi pupil (PUPIL), and it points to YODA only generally as a Jedi teacher; the term is fairly known ('my young Padawan') but leans on fandom vocabulary.
hints.fix: Yoda is the famous Jedi Master who trains young Jedi, including Luke Skywalker.

pairs.pair_note: MASTER may be cleaner for a general audience: Jedi Master Yoda, and master and pupil. The YODA line's parenthetical '(Star Wars fans will know Padawan best)' is confusing and should be dropped.

hints.reason: A dune is a hill of sand, and Dune's desert planet Arrakis is the source of the spice melange; a strong word-plus-franchise double.

pairs.pair_note: 'Only source' is true within the original novel's setting; the recent films keep Dune broadly familiar.

hints.reason: Hermes's famous winged sandals deliver both SHOE (sandals) and WING in one familiar mythological image.

pairs.pair_note: NIKE is a possible alternative (shoe brand, plus Nike the winged goddess of victory) but is not clearly better. HERMES duplicates the FASHION + GOD hint in this batch.

hints.reason: Juliet's 'a rose by any other name would smell as sweet' uses both targets, and roses literally smell sweet too.

pairs.pair_note: Famous line, accurate text.

hints.reason: James Bond the spy and bonds as the investment paired with stocks, a crisp double meaning.
hints.fix: James Bond, 007, is a famous fictional British spy.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the SPY line's 'fiction's most famous spy' is an unsupported superlative, so soften it.

hints.reason: A tied game goes to overtime (TIE), and overtime is extra hours at WORK; two familiar senses of one word.

pairs.pair_note: Good; TIE's necktie sense adds mild misdirection.
